claims.claim: Headline 2030 flexible capacity: 23-27 GW batteries, 4-6 GW LDES, plus 'substantial opportunity' for consumer-led flexibility.
claims.quote: These will be complemented by flexible capacity, including 23-27 GW of battery capacity, 4-6 GW of long‑duration energy storage

claims.claim: Short-duration flexibility is framed as an INCREASE of 29-35 GW from 2023 levels across batteries, consumer-led flexibility and interconnection; it is a capacity increment, not a total.
claims.quote: A significant increase in short‑duration flexibility of 29-35 GW across battery storage, consumer-led flexibility and interconnection capacity from 2023 levels is possible and can play a role in achieving clean power in 2030.

claims.claim: Consumer-led flexibility (CLF) range is 10-12 GW by 2030, excluding electric storage heaters, from 2.5 GW utilised in 2023; EV smart charging expected to drive growth.
claims.quote: Based on NESO and DESNZ scenarios for 2030, excluding electric storage heaters, we expect 10-12 GW of consumer-led flexibility capacity is possible by 2030 to support clean power.

claims.claim: 2023 CLF breakdown: 0.8 GW smart heat pumps and flexible district heating, 0.5 GW EV smart charging, 0.4 GW other smart appliances, 0.8 GW non-domestic.
claims.quote: with 0.8 GW from smart heat pumps and flexible district heating, 0.5 GW from EV smart charging, 0.4 GW from other smart appliances and 0.8 GW from non-domestic consumer-led flexibility.

claims.claim: Definition of CLF: voluntary shifting by consumers, or by Demand Side Response Service Providers on their behalf with consent, while energy needs are still met.
claims.quote: Consumer-led flexibility involves voluntary actions taken freely by energy consumers – or on their behalf by Demand Side Response Service Providers (DSRSPs) with consumers’ consent – to shift some of their electricity use

claims.claim: A separate 40-50 GW of dispatchable and long-duration flexible capacity is needed in 2030; unabated gas retained as back-up.
claims.quote: We are projected to need 40-50 GW[footnote 7] of dispatchable and long‑duration flexible capacity in 2030 to support our power system in extended periods of low renewable output.

claims.claim: The plan promised a Low Carbon Flexibility Roadmap the following year (published July 2025 as the Clean Flexibility Roadmap).
claims.quote: A Low Carbon Flexibility Roadmap will be published next year, with new actions to drive clean power flexibility by 2030.

sources.harvard: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Ofgem and National Energy System Operator (2025) Clean flexibility roadmap. July. London: DESNZ. Available at: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/clean-flexibility-roadmap/clean-flexibility-roadmap (accessed 7 November 2026).

claims.claim: The total 2030 clean-flexibility range is 51-66 GW, a two- to three-fold increase on 24 GW installed in 2023. This is the headline 'total flex' number.
claims.quote: The Plan set out a flexibility capacity range of 51 GW to 66 GW by 2030, marking a two to three-fold increase on the 24 GW of capacity installed in 2023.
claims.locator: 'Introduction' (context on the Clean Power 2030 Action Plan)

claims.claim: The roadmap restates the short-duration increment as 28-36 GW, which differs from the 29-35 GW printed in the Action Plan itself; cite the Action Plan for the official range.
claims.quote: the ‘Clean Power 2030 Action Plan’ confirmed that a significant increase of 28 GW to 36 GW in short duration[footnote 18] flexibility from 2023 levels is possible
claims.locator: 'What is short duration vs long duration flexibility?'

claims.claim: Table 1 (2024 baseline / CPAP 2030 / FES 2025 Holistic Transition 2030 / 2050): total CLF 1.6 / 10-12 / 10.3 / 74.6 GW; hybrid heat pumps 0.0 / - / 0.0 / 0.2 GW; smart charging 0.2 / - / 2.7 / 10.1 GW; batteries 6.8 / 23-27 / 23.2 / 39.3 GW. NESO's scenario expects no hybrid heat pump flexibility in 2030.
claims.quote: Table 1: 2030 and 2050 indicative flexibility capacity by technology scenarios, GW
claims.locator: Table 1 (values read from the table rows)

claims.quote: DESNZ to appoint a Flexibility Commissioner, as part of the Clean Power 2030 Advisory Commission, in 2025.

claims.quote: The government appointed Cathy McClay as Flexibility Commissioner in December 2025 to accelerate clean flexibility delivery across boundaries.

claims.claim: NESO's first-year target of 170 MW of new CLF dispatchable in its markets (BM and DFS) was met; target 750 MW of I&C flexibility in NESO markets by 2030. These are small against a 10-12 GW ambition.
claims.quote: Year 1 target met: NESO’s Power Responsive can report that 170MW of new CLF is now dispatchable across its markets (specifically BM and DFS).

claims.quote: UKRI has committed £74m to the CLF Challenge, aiming to deliver at least 2GW of flexibility by 2030.

claims.claim: Bids 10,983.5 MWh, accepted 5,449.6 MWh; accepted tenders GBP 1,223,312 (p.3) or GBP 1,233,312 (p.16): the report is internally inconsistent; settled spend GBP 943,983.
claims.quote: During this winter period NESO received 10,983.5MWh of bids, with 5,449.6MWh accepted. This equates to a total of £1,223,312 tenders accepted. We paid out £943,983 for delivered volume.
claims.locator: Executive Summary, p.3; cf. Financial Summary, p.16

claims.quote: Overall, the average accepted bid price across all accepted bids was £210/MWh. The lowest accepted bid price was £59 on 27 December 2024 for 1MW covering 1 SP.

claims.claim: The Guaranteed Acceptance Price was retained in the terms but never issued in 2024/25, so there was no guaranteed price that winter.
claims.quote: The Service Terms and Procurement Rules retained the concept of test events and Guaranteed Acceptance Price, but neither were issued during the winter period.

claims.claim: Day-ahead procurement removed: DFS is now within-day only.
claims.quote: NESO removed the day ahead procurement option to support our ambition to move as close to real time procurement as possible aligning to a compliant product.

claims.claim: Domestic delivery stays tiny and manual: 91% of domestic delivery below 1 kW; >99% of MPANs manually initiated; ~60/40 domestic/I&C split by volume.
claims.quote: 91% of delivery was below 1kW, and 9% between 1kW and 10kW. These figures are consistent with previous winters.

claims.claim: Frequent events made baselining harder early in the season, an admission that event frequency erodes the baseline.
claims.quote: The frequent use of DFS during winter made it challenging for some parties to establish an accurate baseline early in the season.

claims.claim: Domestic DFS baseline = BSC P376 BL01 WITHOUT the in-day adjustment (self-nomination only for I&C/generation).
claims.quote: the methodology outlined in BSC P376 'Utilising a Baselining Methodology to set Physical Notifications’ (methodology id: BL01) ... will be applied ... but without the final in day adjustment

claims.claim: BL01: eligible days are same-type days in the 60-day window D-60..D-1, with HH data, not Event Days, not clock-change days.
claims.quote: Step 1 of the BL01 process is to identify the historical Settlement Days (in the sixty-day window from day D–60 to day D–1) that will be used to calculate the DFS Operational Baseline.

claims.claim: Working day: the ten most recent eligible days (5-9 if fewer; <5 = no baseline). Non-working day: four most recent, middle two by daily volume. Baseline = arithmetic mean per settlement period. (Step 2 text says 'six to ten', Table 2 says 'five to nine': internal inconsistency.)
claims.quote: selected (four for a Non-Working Day, and up to ten for a Working Day)
claims.locator: Schedule 3, Part 3, Table 2 and Step 2, p.35

claims.claim: Event days excluded from the baseline include DFS acceptances, DNO flexibility instructions, Capacity Market delivery and NESO trials, so each event day drops out of the next baseline.
claims.quote: An Event Day for these purposes is a Settlement Day containing a Settlement Period in respect of which:-

claims.quote: with respect to all DFS Tests, DFS Submissions for which the Utilisation Price is at or below the Guaranteed Acceptance Price will not be assessed and NESO will issue DFS Acceptances
